source.title: Structured Features Overfit Where Random Features Grok
source.authors: Chon-Fai Kam; M. Bessafi; Frédéric Cadet

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests capacity and training-time behavior in a structured-feature ridge model and reports results that challenge the expected generalization and grokking behavior in that setting.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own feature-band capacity sweep, active-mode masking sweep, and one training trajectory. Results cited from Xu et al. and other prior work are not rows. The unrepresentable target ab in Table 1 is excluded because it does not test behavior for a target in the model class. The numerical Table 1 results for representable targets are included separately from the main dynamical sweep.
record.test_reason: The capacity sweep of held-out accuracy crosses the interpolation threshold (q/n from 0.364 to 1.744) in a linear ridge read-out over a structured Fourier feature map. That is a new model class and setting with a direct result on whether risk improves past interpolation (V4). The study's aim is grokking, not double descent, and the authors state their result is distinct from double descent. The one training trajectory bears weakly on V2. The masking sweep measures a related construct (active support versus nominal dimension) and fits no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add that the authors explicitly say the collapse is not an interpolation effect: it begins at q/n = 0.638, below threshold. They call their result compatible with but distinct from double descent, and say it concerns whether a grokking delay appears, not where the test-error curve sits.
record.recipe_differences: The cited comparison uses unstructured identity or Gaussian random features; this study uses a fixed structured Fourier-character band, a linear read-out, p = 97, and fixed positive weight decay λ = 10−2. It is not a reproduction of the original deep-network experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome changes with active support: at nominal M = 32, masking to 1089 modes yields 1.000 held-out accuracy, while the full 4225-mode band yields 0.185. The capacity sweep also reports degradation beginning below q/n = 1. Only one λ and one training sample size are used in the main experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed nominal dimension M = 32, masking to at most 1089 active modes gives 1.000 held-out accuracy, while the full 4225-mode band gives 0.185. Masked and unmasked sweeps coincide on an active-mode axis.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In structured feature maps, generalization is governed by the active (signal-free) support via the teacher-weighted Gram spectrum, not by nominal parameter count.

record.code_released: available from the authors upon request
record.peer_reviewed: OPT2026: 18th Annual Workshop on Optimization for Machine Learning
record.problems: The main dynamical results use one target, one training-set size, one weight decay, and three seeds. The trajectory diagnostic is one seed at one band radius. The reported peak accuracy is an upper envelope over training rather than terminal accuracy. The study does not test deep jointly trained networks, sample-size dependence, or a regularization sweep.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 rows for the unrepresentable target ab are omitted because the paper states that ab is not in the feature class at any finite band radius; those results do not test the reported generalization behavior for a representable target.

untested.parts: All: no deep networks; the jointly trained two-layer case is explicitly out of scope.
Epoch-wise behaviour near or above the interpolation threshold, multiple seeds, deep networks.
All: n is fixed at 3763; no sample-size sweep.
Capacities beyond q/n = 1.744, other λ values including λ → 0, other targets and model classes.
All: no peak location across size, epochs or samples. The c(λ)·n threshold heuristic is untested in n and λ by the authors' own statement.
All: no noise or regularization sweep; λ = 1e-2 throughout the dynamical runs.
All: no second descent arises to be re-expressed under an effective parameter count.

missing.what: Preliminary λ = 0 observation of a long memorize-then-generalize separation at the band radii that collapse at λ = 1e-2. Text only, no numbers; it bears on regularization dependence of the collapse.

record.verdict_notes: The study's target is grokking (Xu et al.), not double descent; double-descent relevance comes from the capacity sweep crossing q/n = 1. Measure is peak-over-training held-out accuracy, an upper envelope, not terminal test error. Only one λ (1e-2), one n, one single-mode target, three seeds, and capacities only to q/n = 1.744, so a later second descent or a different λ outcome cannot be excluded. R12 duplicates R5. Table 1 closed-form rows are representability checks and were unlinked from V4 and V7.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies feature dimension in a linear read-out over a fixed feature map, not model size in deep networks; the jointly trained two-layer case is explicitly outside scope.

Only one trajectory is reported, at M = 24, λ = 10−2, and one seed. The text describes the plateau after about 10,000 steps and the absence of a late rise, but does not specify the complete fall-rise-fall curve over training.
Training sample size is fixed at n = 3763 in the main experiments; no sample-size sweep is reported.
Only a structured character-feature linear read-out and one task are tested; the study does not establish a general result across model classes.

The study does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts a peak across size, epochs, and sample count. It fixes sample size and weight decay, and reports no peak location across those axes.
The main dynamical experiments use λ = 10−2; there is no noise sweep, regularization sweep, or test of multiple peaks or optimally tuned regularization.

The study tests active-mode counts against nominal dimension in its structured-feature setting, but does not show that an existing second-descent curve becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve under a different parameter count.

rows.subject: linear read-out over the symmetric Laurent band character feature map
rows.stage_stated: training trajectory; λ = 10−2; ν = 5; learning rate 0.05
rows.operation_detail: Track held-out accuracy during training at 100-step intervals.
rows.value: Reaches its ceiling of 0.91 by about step 10,000 and then stays flat; no late upswing is reported.
rows.note: The authors say the trajectory does not show the late rise that would indicate delayed generalization. The text does not describe the entire test-error curve.
rows.check: Held-out accuracy rises to 0.91 by about step 10,000, then stays flat to about 25,000 steps: no rise-then-fall in error. The run is under-parameterized (q/n = 0.638), one seed, one λ. The record framed it as grokking (late generalization), which is a different construct from V2.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for the complete V2 shape from the supplied text. Accuracy reaches 0.91 by approximately step 10,000 and remains flat during the second half of the roughly 25,000-step diagnostic; no late grokking transition occurs.
